_meta.framing: C-SSRS-informed risk language; 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (US); Crisis Text Line; Samaritans for UK/IE; Lifeline for AU

safety_protocol.name: Safety Protocol
safety_protocol.description: Triggered when the user shows signs of suicidal ideation or self-harm.
mandatory_elements: Provide crisis resources (988, Crisis Text Line)
Express willingness to stay with them
Do not try to quickly fix the problem
safety_protocol.emergency_note: If there is an immediate risk of harm, please call 911 (US/CA), 999 (UK), 000 (AU), or local emergency services.

phase1_acknowledgment: I hear how heavy this feels right now. You don't have to pretend it's okay.
Thank you for telling me. I know saying these words takes courage.
What you're carrying sounds really painful. I want you to know — you are not alone with this.
I noticed you mentioned {keyword}. I want to check in gently — are you having thoughts of hurting yourself tonight?
phase2_validation: Saying this out loud, in this much pain, takes a lot of strength.
These feelings of wanting things to end — they may have been with you for a long time.
However hopeless it feels right now, there are people trained to help you find a way through.
You don't need to have an answer tonight. I'm here with you until you're ready.
phase3_resources:
I want to share some support right now:

📞 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (US): call or text 988
💬 Crisis Text Line: text HOME to 741741

Both are free, confidential, and staffed 24/7 by trained counselors.

If you're outside the US:

🇬🇧 Samaritans (UK/IE): 116 123
🇦🇺 Lifeline (AU): 13 11 14
🌐 Find your country: befrienders.org
If you feel you're in immediate danger, please call 911 (US/CA), 999 (UK), 000 (AU), or your local emergency number — or go to the nearest emergency room.
phase4_grounding: Let's come back to right now. Where are you? Are you at home, somewhere safe?
Let's do something small together — feel your feet on the floor. Notice the weight of your body resting on whatever is holding you up.
Right now, in this moment — can you name one thing you can see, one thing you can hear, and one thing you can feel? Take your time.

continuation_responses.description: How to keep the conversation open after the safety protocol triggers.
templates: I'm right here. Keep talking, or just sit with me — either is okay.
It helps that you're still here, still talking to me. I'm not going anywhere.
You don't have to carry this alone. We can keep this connection as long as you need.
If talking feels like too much, just tell me one word for how you feel right now.

transfer_responses.description: Language for gently moving the user toward human support.
templates: I think a trained crisis counselor could help you in a way I can't. They've sat with this exact kind of pain many times.
Would you be willing to text or call 988 right now? You can keep this chat open at the same time.
If picking up the phone feels too much, you can text 988 or text HOME to 741741 — it's quieter, and you can take your time.

follow_up_script.description: Gentle check-in after a safety event has resolved.
session_check_in: How have things felt since we last talked?
Were you able to reach out to anyone for support?
How are you doing right now? Has anything shifted, even a little?
positive_reinforcement: Coming back here, after a night like that, is itself a kind of strength.
However tonight feels, the fact that you keep showing up is worth honoring.
